LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FORMAL LETTER

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: which formal information was passed on during the pre-colonial days. Why do we write letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify components of a formal letter for information
2. compose a formal letter using correct format for communication
3. appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FORMAL LETTER
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FORMAL LETTER
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify components of a formal letter for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify components of a formal letter for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify components of a formal letter for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify components of a formal letter for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose a formal letter using correct format for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a formal letter using correct format for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a formal letter using correct format for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a formal letter using correct format for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify components of a formal letter for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter to a partner. (skill: compose a formal letter using correct format for communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify components of a formal letter for information.
3. Practise this skill: compose a formal letter using correct format for communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of formal letters to communicate in real life situations.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. which formal information was passed on during the pre-colonial days. Why do we write letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Formal Letter means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify components of a formal letter for information.
5. Be able to: compose a formal letter using correct format for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
